title: CFPB Ordered Cash App Parent Block to Pay Up to $175 Million
alt_title_1: Why Cash App's Support Number Sent Fraud Victims to Voicemail
alt_title_2: Inside the $175M CFPB Order Over Cash App Fraud Disputes
description_hook: In Consent Order 2025-CFPB-0001, the Consumer Financial Protection Bureau ordered Cash App parent Block, Inc. to pay up to $120 million in consumer redress plus a $55 million civil penalty over fraud-investigation and customer-support failures. Block consented without admitting or denying the findings.

scenes.headline: Up to $175M CFPB Order on Block
scenes.narration: The CFPB ordered Cash App's parent company, Block, to pay up to 175 million dollars over how it handled fraud on the app.
scenes.source: In the Matter of Block, Inc., 2025-CFPB-0001, p. 1 (Jan 16, 2025)

scenes.headline: Card Number Played a Recording
scenes.narration: Until 2021, the number on the back of Cash Cards played a recording with no live agent, pushing victims toward fake support numbers online.

scenes.headline: Fought 75% of Bank Chargebacks
scenes.narration: When users asked their banks to reverse unauthorized peer-to-peer transfers, the CFPB found Block challenged at least 75 percent of those chargebacks.

scenes.headline: Up to $120M Back to Users
scenes.narration: Without admitting or denying the findings, Block agreed to up to 120 million dollars in user redress, a 55 million penalty, and live phone support.

scenes.headline: Apps Are Wallets, Not Vaults
scenes.right_body: Keep real savings off P2P apps
scenes.narration: Use payment apps like cash in your pocket, not a vault. Sweep idle balances straight back to an insured bank account.
